svg.aria-label: Architecture of the Open Trading Surface event-processing subsystem: event plane, condition layer, rule layer, action layer, strategy layer and backtester, with refusal points marked distinctly.
svg.title: Event processing — events, conditions, rules, actions, strategies, backtests
svg.desc: Derived from the shipped code at 5.43.0: server/event-registry.js, event-log.js, event-producers.js, data-change.js, condition.js, condition-eval.js, condition-env.js, rules.js, rule-state.js, rule-engine.js, rule-accrual.js, rule-actions.js, paper-book.js, strategy*.js, backtest-strategy.js, backtest-rerun.js, backtest-store.js, deflation.js, search-ledger.js, membership-ledger.js.

g.text: Event processing — the CEP engine, the strategy layer and the backtester
Open Trading Surface · derived from the shipped code, not from the specification · every box names the module that owns it
the happy path — a value, a record or a control flows
A REFUSAL — it names what is missing and writes nothing
registered in the vocabulary, and nothing writes it
refusal point — the run stops here rather than defaulting
a writer exists and rides a fetch that was already happening
a writer exists, but only runs if a key / a process / a gesture does
the kind resolves in the registry and no producer has ever written it — a rule on it cannot fire
The event plane — one vocabulary, two timestamps, an append-only log
PRODUCERS — NO POLLING LOOP EXISTS. EVERY ONE RIDES A FETCH THAT WAS ALREADY HAPPENING.
facts only — no sentiment, importance, category or relevance
door: get_events → events.aggregate — ON DEMAND ONLY, no schedule
the classification is the intake's, from STRUCTURED FIELDS ONLY
Data change — detected against a WATERMARK
server/data-change.js — never a cache, never a poll
The engine's own record — written by bands C, D and E
EVERY FAMILY IS BUILT from a vocabulary its own
producer publishes. Nothing here restates a list,
and a coverage test fails the build BOTH ways.
Seven planes, each with a different answer to
on a kind the registry does not carry, naming the
families it could have meant. Never coerced.
21 of the 101 kinds resolve in the registry and
NO CODE PATH RECORDS THEM. A rule matching one
compiles, saves, ticks daily and cannot fire.
None of the four requires server/event-log.js.
not happened; the log pages BACKWARDS, so
recently" answer with things that have not.
a dated range — the evaluator's door
pages BACKWARDS from the newest day
what has EVER been written, live
an explicit null means NEVER knowable, and is honoured
Matching reads observed_at: an event becomes true on
the first bar at or after it became knowable — and every
EVENT_MAX_BYTES 4096 bounds the WRITE, never the detection:
an oversized payload is cut to its first three keys and SAYS
· a missing source — an event with no source cannot be
joined back to the artifact that produced it
turns the throw into a STATED REFUSAL. Every producer uses
it, so a log write can never cost the read it rides on.
Where a rule reads it — condition-env.js
THE KNOWABILITY CUT: the environment is assembled from
bars ≤ t and events with observed_at ≤ close(t), and from
nothing else. An event whose observed_at is null is NEVER
knowable and is EXCLUDED rather than dated by occurrence.
What it does not fetch is as deliberate as what it does: a
condition naming no cohort does not touch the ledger, and the
provenance block says which sources were skipped.
IDEMPOTENCE IS REFUSAL TO APPEND, never an edit: a re-run
The dedupe check and the append are ONE operation under
store.withLock — splitting them is exactly how two
writers both find the key absent and both write it.
A per-day key index advances from the byte offset it last
read to, so a re-fetch costs O(new lines).
A crash-truncated tail is detected UNDER THE LOCK and
NO RETENTION POLICY, NO PRUNE VERB, NO CAP. The log and
the accrual record are the forward point-in-time evidence,
and pruning them destroys the only such evidence the
It carries the SUBJECT. The stores that invented the key were
per-symbol, so the subject was implicit in the filename; a
cross-subject key without it silently eats records.
The log does not become the authority for anything. Every
producer KEEPS ITS OWN STORE as the authority for its own
surface — the divergence view reads its ledger, the repricing
report reads its run files — and the log is the JOIN beside
them. Nothing was deleted or rewritten to build it.
the browsable stream, filtered by kind,
plane, subject or date, with its cursor
replays what is already on disk;
The condition layer — a tree over predicate streams
The sugar is REGENERATED from the JSON on every write, so the
display text cannot drift from the stored object. A stored
string would be a parser dependency forever.
Six leaf kinds — each resolves in a registry, or refuses
expr-series.compileSeries over BARS only — a stray
non-bar identifier is refused by name
the ONE indicator registry, parameters its own
index and universe membership are NOT offered
the per-subject named state a set_state action wrote
Every leaf carries its PLANE, which is what the point-in-time gate consults.
Eight combinators — the temporal operators CEP requires
three-valued: an unknown leaf is null and propagates
SEQUENCE — ordered, and the window is REQUIRED
max | min | sum | avg of a series expression
held across a window; at_least k makes it N-of-M
NEGATION WITH TIMEOUT — fires at the EXPIRY of its
window, ON A DAY WHEN NOTHING HAPPENED. This is
what makes the engine a SCHEDULER, not a filter.
Windows: sliding (default) · tumbling size · session gap
20 TRADING days (bars) — a holiday is not a bar
20 CALENDAR days — a holiday consumes one
A BARE NUMBER IS A PARSE ERROR, and the
refusal NAMES BOTH SUFFIXES. There is no
default, and there will not be one.
every bar it holds — requires an explicit
debounce, refused at save; a level rule
It runs BEFORE the evaluation is believed, and
its verdicts ride the payload whether or not
Eleven families, each a LIVE READ of the stores.
A verdict changes the day the record is long
enough, with nobody editing a constant.
The EVALUATOR refuses on its own account too, which
is a stronger statement: a FIELD leaf reads the
CURRENT screener row, so at any historical as_of it
refuses. A `gated` verdict says the record COULD
support it; the evaluator says whether THIS READER
can, and the two are reported separately.
THE COMPILER REFUSES AT SAVE, NOT AT 3 A.M.
· a leaf that resolves in NO registry — naming every registry searched and their sizes
· a bare duration · a level trigger with no debounce · an unbounded then sequence
· an absent with no anchor — "B never happened" is a claim about all of history, not a rule
· more than CONDITION_MAX_NODES (64) · a trading window past CONDITION_WINDOW_MAX_BARS (2520)
· => — an action is not part of a condition; the refusal explains the state key and points at the rule
THE KNOWABILITY CUT LIVES HERE, which is why it is a module and not four lines in a handler: the environment is assembled from bars ≤ t and
events with observed_at ≤ close(t), and from nothing else. An event with observed_at null is NEVER knowable and is EXCLUDED rather than
dated by its occurrence. Bars may be INJECTED by a caller that has already cut them — which is the seam the strategy loop and the replay use.
WHAT IT DOES NOT FETCH IS AS DELIBERATE AS WHAT IT DOES: a condition naming no field does not run the screener; one naming no event does not
read the log; one naming no cohort does not touch the ledger — and the provenance block says which sources were consulted, and which were skipped.
The rule layer — a named, versioned condition with a subject scope
SCOPE IS REQUIRED. Defaulting it to the universe would
silently point a per-name evaluation at six thousand names.
The per-subject state, and the version law
It holds the sequence PARTIALS, the live absent TIMERS, the edge
trigger's last value, the debounce clock and the named states.
An edit that MOVES the fingerprint — the condition — bumps
rule_version and RESETS the state, archiving what it drops to the
log as book.rule.reset. A partial is a claim about a condition, and
continuing it under new semantics would produce a firing no reading
An edit that does not — name, note, scope, playbook, enabled,
ACTIONS — INHERITS. Renaming a rule must not re-arm it.
Once per weekday, CALENDAR-TRIGGERED with a data preference.
IT TICKS ON EMPTY DAYS BY DESIGN.
An absent … within N fires at the EXPIRY of its window, on a day
when nothing happened — so a data-triggered tick would be silent
on the one day it was needed, and a missed tick is a MISSED FIRING
that leaves no other trace anywhere.
"RAN, NOTHING FIRED" is a recorded SUCCESS in those words. Silence
records nothing, and nothing reads RED past
subjects; the pending list persists, so a halt RESUMES.
CAPS THAT REFUSE, WITH THEIR COUNT
Each is recorded as book.rule.refused. A refusal that is
not recorded is indistinguishable from a rule that did not fire.
refused WHOLE, never over a prefix — a firing count over
Also refused per leg: a predicate with no point-in-time
value at the requested as_of, naming the leg, its plane
EVERY LIVE EVALUATION WRITES A DATED ROW WHETHER OR NOT IT FIRED. THE NON-FIRINGS ARE THE DATA.
A record of only the fires cannot compute a hit rate, a base rate or a false-positive count — the three things a reader actually wants
to know about a rule after a year. And most of the interesting predicates here cannot be reconstructed backwards at all; a rule written
TODAY writes, every trading day from today, the value those predicates ACTUALLY HAD — observed, not reconstructed.
COVERAGE COUNTS DAYS, NOT ROWS. A rule ticking over 40 names for 3 days has 120 rows and THREE DAYS of record; reporting 120 would be
cross-section wearing a time series' clothes. ACCRUAL_MIN_DAYS_FOR_REACH = 60. No retention policy, no prune verb, no cap.
Read it with get_rule_evaluations (fired: true | false | omit for both) and get_rule_history.
What a firing does, in order
Provenance is captured AT FIRING TIME and never resolved later: the rule id, name, fingerprint and version
are the ones in force when it fired. A proposal that re-read its rule at display time would silently restate
its own reason after an edit.
test_rule runs this whole evaluation with NO SIDE EFFECTS — no event, no accrual row, no state, no notification, no fire count.
The action layer — what a firing CAUSES
ACTIONS ATTACH TO THE RULE, NOT TO THE CONDITION
The condition's fingerprint is the per-subject state key. If an action were
part of the condition, RETAGGING A PROPOSAL would re-arm the rule on every
name it watches. So the sugar accepts =>, the actions are stored
BESIDE the condition, and condition.fingerprint never sees them.
An action edit therefore INHERITS state.
One registry; the selector and the tool surface both derive from it.
size (7 arms), tag, limit (RECORDED, never enforced)
target_pct of total equity — the DELTA trade
label + one of five disclosure severities
through notes.add — THE ONE note store, unchanged
see the two panels to the right
Writes a book.* event back into the log, which a LATER
TICK may match. An emitted event is written NOW and
matched later, never re-evaluated inside this tick.
REFUSES: an unregistered kind; ANY PLANE BUT book — a rule
emitting a filing.* or tape.* kind would be this installation
asserting a fact about the world on its own authority;
a chain past CASCADE_MAX_DEPTH (3); and — statically, at
SAVE time — a rule that emits a kind it also MATCHES,
which is a rule that fires itself forever.
set_state — the writer the state leaf needed
Wave 1 compiled {"state":…} and refused to evaluate it
because nothing wrote one. This is the writer; the store is
a STORE bound, not a policy — the strategy's own
max_positions is band E, and it also decides WHICH
A REAL portfolio.js ledger in every respect except one: it is
marked paper, it lives in its own file, and NOTHING in this system
can write a proposal into anything else.
It gets the same lot engine, the same five cost-basis methods, the
same corporate-action vocabulary and the same analytics.reconcile
self-test — deliberately, so the proposals can be read honestly
through the existing report and the paginated PDF.
ONE BOOK PER STRATEGY — comparisons need independence.
Every transaction carries proposed:true, a why naming the rule,
the version, the fingerprint and the firing, and an origin block.
get_paper_book, delete_paper_book. That is the whole list.
There is deliberately no promote_paper_book, no order verb
and no execute verb. The owner books a trade by booking a trade.
WHAT AN ACTION REFUSES OR SKIPS
· propose_sell on a name the book does not hold. A sell of an
unheld name is not a smaller sell — booking it would open a
SHORT LOT, and this engine has no short-lot concept.
· a rule that names no paper book, refused at SAVE
· a real portfolio named as the target — refused BY NAME, with
the sentence that names it as the owner's own ledger. "Not
found" would read as a typo, which is what invites a retry.
no close on the firing bar
a quote missing for any held name
a shared-budget size arm on a book no strategy owns
IT NEVER FALLS BACK TO A DEFAULT WEIGHT.
The strategy layer — firings compete for cash, slots, sector budget and liquidity
roles: entry · exit · adjust · veto — the role is
the STRATEGY's, so one rule can be one strategy's
the rule tick — the loop reads what the rules found,
so running it first would form positions from
Sizing — every arm states its BUDGET BASIS
a share of WHAT, because that is the question a reader of a size has
NO SHARED BUDGET — WORKS ON ANY PAPER BOOK
a share of TOTAL EQUITY, fully marked
SHARED BUDGET — REFUSES ON A BOOK NO STRATEGY OWNS
a fixed fraction of equity PUT AT RISK
No shorting, no leverage, no margin. risk_parity's scale is
capped at fully-invested and NAMES ITSELF when it binds.
Constraints — this ORDER, and they COMPOSE
WHEN ONE BINDS, THE PAYLOAD NAMES WHICH ONE — plus
every other that would also have bound.
On any day where more candidates signal than fit,
SOMETHING decides which get the cash and the slots. If
the strategy does not say, the answer is hash iteration
order — a hidden choice that changes the result and that
nobody would defend if it were written down.
screen row — anything a screen selects on
A NULL RANK IS "no value for the thing you are ranking on",
not "ranks zero". Nulls sort LAST and are COUNTED.
Exact ties break on signal time, then symbol — legal HERE
only because it is declared, bounded and REPORTED per row.
THE EDIT LAW — AND IT DIFFERS FROM A RULE'S, DELIBERATELY
A FORMING edit (universe, rules, policy) moves the formation fingerprint, bumps strategy_version and writes a DATED METHODOLOGY BREAK
(book.strategy.policy_changed) — and DOES NOT RESET THE BOOK. A rule's partial match is a CLAIM about a condition and means nothing under
new semantics; a book is a RECORD of proposals actually made at prices that actually printed, and resetting it would delete the only
out-of-sample evidence the strategy has. An equity curve spanning a break is MORE THAN ONE MEASUREMENT, and every payload says so.
Cash yield — and the payload SAYS WHICH WAS USED
Accrued actual/360 — the US money-market convention for bills — and booked as interest transactions, so the EXISTING income
accounting in portfolio.derive() and the gross/net TWR in analytics.js handle it, rather than a parallel path.
the 3-month bill, fred:DTB3, where a FRED key is configured · zero where it is not. NEVER A SILENT DEFAULT.
The daily loop — server/strategy-loop.js run() · THE ORDER IS THE CONTRACT AND IT IS NOT NEUTRAL

The loop takes a CLOCK and reads the wall clock NOWHERE — liveClock | fixedClock | replayClock. A derived test fails the build on a new Date() inside the walk, because the backtester DRIVES this same function.
a split applied after the signal would price the
before any trade — interest on the opening balance
is earned whatever the day then does with it
bars ≤ t, events observed_at ≤ close(t), and nothing
else — then the mark every later step reads
removes a subject from ENTRY and is RECORDED: "no
signal" and "signalled but vetoed" are different
BEFORE ENTRIES — an exit frees cash AND a slot;
entries first tie capacity to iteration order
candidates collected, then ranked by the strategy's
in rank order until something binds; each miss records
skipped_capacity WITH ITS BINDING CONSTRAINT NAMED
at the bar CLOSE, cost_bps per side booked as a `fee`
transaction — not a second cost path
if t is a rebalance date, through
analytics.reconcile derives the day two independent
ways and THROWS above one cent. NO FLAG SKIPS IT.
The backtest — the SAME loop, a replay clock, and a bias toward refusing over producing a number
1 · PREFLIGHT — IT COLLECTS EVERY REFUSAL, NOT THE FIRST
SURVIVORSHIP a cohort-, screen- or universe-scoped historical run is
REFUSED, naming the missing dated ledger. An EXPLICIT list runs, with the
caller's own selection bias disclosed as the caller's own.
POINT-IN-TIME any leg whose verdict is gated · recorded_days ·
forward_only · unresolved refuses the run, NAMING the leg, the rule and the plane.
THE RANK a rank over a screen field is REFUSED — 2019's candidates by 2026's
fundamentals is not a subtle bias, it is the answer. Permitted: signal_time,
random(seed), expressions over close. GENERATIONS refused unless acknowledged.
2 · THE REPLAY — the SAME loop, a different clock
A BACKTEST IS NOT A SIMULATOR. It is strategy-loop.run() — the loop
the live book runs — under a replay clock, writing real
portfolio.buildRec records into a PAPER BOOK OF ITS OWN,
It never touches the strategy's live forward book: that record is
the out-of-sample evidence hindsight cannot manufacture.
It computes NO return, NO Sharpe, NO drawdown and NO attribution of
its own — every number comes from an EXISTING module: analytics.js,
result is computed — a run that registered
only on success would count the winners and
below it → Šidák, AND IT SAYS WHICH.
A REFUSED run registers NOTHING: nothing ran.
The deflation asks HOW MANY THINGS YOU TRIED.
This asks HOW MUCH OF IT WAS ONE LUCKY NAME.
Same strategy, same window, the top
A DROP RE-RUN IS NOT A TRIAL.
It registers as a DERIVED record and does not
move the denominator — or the more carefully a
result was checked, the worse it would read.
LAW 4 — PROPOSALS ONLY, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL IN FOUR PLACES, NOT CONVENTIONAL IN ONE
1 · a DIFFERENT FILE — <statedir>/paper-books.json, never portfolios.json, with a throw if the two paths ever resolve to the same bytes
2 · the write path CANNOT ADDRESS a real book: it resolves targets only inside the paper store, and naming a real portfolio is REFUSED BY NAME
3 · only the PURE functions of portfolio.js are reached — asserted by reading both module graphs
4 · paper:true is stamped AT THE WRITE, not asserted at the read, and rides every payload

svg.text: There is no execute verb, no order verb, no broker and no promote_paper_book anywhere in this system. · Diagram derived from the shipped code at 5.43.0; where the specification and the code disagree, the code is what is drawn.
